page: Amazon Web Services c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. Cache distribution comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory resources total 8.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, reflecting a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 vector extensions, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong single-threaded performance, with stress-ng single-core execution and Geekbench single-core tests placing in the upper quartile. Instruction extensions provide high throughput on text processing and bzip3 decompression tasks. In contrast, multi-core metrics, including PassMark CPU and multi-threaded decompression, reside within the middle quartile. Memory subsystem evaluation reveals a performance divergence: cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaches 591.1 GB/sec, while uncached large-block 256 MB reads reach 37.76 GB/sec and PassMark memory tests place in the lower quartile.

The c7a.xlarge instance lacks local NVMe storage and included GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for non-volatile data and operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The dense single-thread processing capabilities offer high operational efficiency for compute-bound applications that do not depend on high local I/O throughput or extensive memory capacity. This configuration fits batch computational pipelines, software compilation via Clang, continuous integration runners, algorithmic simulation, and distributed web service nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores at 3.7 GHz and 8.0 GB of DDR5 system memory at 5 GHz, the instance delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suited for CPU-bound tasks. It integrates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, BF16, and VAES. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core execution speeds in Geekbench and stress-ng, accompanied by average multi-core and weak large-block uncached memory bandwidth. Operating with 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware, c7a.xlarge delivers cost-efficient compute capacity for workloads such as continuous integration, Clang software builds, distributed batch compute, and static web serving nodes that do not demand extensive RAM pools.
